fixes.was: [redacted supplier-specific title]
fixes.now: Government technology supplier dependency under scrutiny
fixes.reason: Names the dominant theme supported by the briefing's items without an unsupported claim of increasing scrutiny or references excluded from public publication.

fixes.was: [redacted supplier-specific framing]; written answers were dominated by questions about government dependence on single technology suppliers
fixes.now: Written answers cover government technology supplier dependency, exit planning and open standards, alongside departmental AI model assurance.
fixes.reason: The selected items support this theme, but the evidence does not establish that it dominated all written answers.

fixes.was: Anthropic's and OpenAI's compute credits for the AI Biosecurity Lab; made up the rest of the day's relevant business
fixes.now: OpenAI's compute and model credits and Anthropic's model credits for the AI Biosecurity Lab; Other items cover data-centre energy and regulation, cyber security, digital literacy and committee publications.
fixes.reason: Anthropic's contribution is described as model credits, not compute credits. The original summary also implied an exhaustive account that omitted several of its own items.

fixes.was: [redacted supplier-specific wording]
fixes.now: Departments outline AI model controls; China assurance questions tabled
fixes.reason: Retained the evidenced departmental controls and questions while removing references excluded from public publication. Approved technology providers should not be described as necessarily developing the models.

fixes.was: the work to assure the security of AI models from China, which the AI Minister mentioned in the House on 26 November
fixes.now: His questions refer to security-assurance work on AI models from China mentioned by the Minister for Artificial Intelligence in the House on 26 November.
fixes.reason: The reference to the earlier ministerial remarks is supplied in the questions, not in a transcript of those remarks.

fixes.was: Model provenance and sovereignty are becoming explicit tests in departmental assurance. If the China-model assurance results are shared with business, they could feed into procurement criteria that favour trusted, assured platforms.
fixes.now: The answers describe departmental AI checks and the MoD's security and sovereignty considerations. The newly tabled questions seek details of China-model assurance work; no answers are supplied.
fixes.reason: Removed unsupported claims about a policy trend, future procurement criteria and predicted follow-up questions.

fixes.was: Mr Wrigley tabled a series of questions on the Palantir-run Federated Data Platform (FDP), whose contract expires in March 2029.
fixes.now: Mr Wrigley's 11 questions, tabled on 18 November and answered on 27 November, concern Palantir's Federated Data Platform (FDP). His questions refer to the contract's expiry in March 2029.
fixes.reason: Distinguished tabling from answering, used the evidenced supplier relationship, and attributed the expiry date to the questions.

fixes.was: an assurance that no further NHS bodies will be required to adopt it
fixes.now: steps to ensure that no additional NHS organisation is required to adopt it during the period to March 2029
fixes.reason: Restored the question's time limit rather than implying an indefinite restriction.

fixes.was: The FDP successor procurement is shaping up as a major public-sector data and AI platform competition, and the criteria being pressed for ... will set expectations for any bidder, including hyperscale cloud providers.
fixes.now: The questions seek open standards, interoperability, independent assurance and supplier neutrality. The answers do not confirm these as procurement requirements and defer further details.
fixes.reason: Requests from an MP are not confirmed procurement criteria; the evidence does not establish bidders or the competition's scale.

fixes.was: A short, final Fujitsu extension is in place while Accenture takes over Horizon support.
fixes.now: The answer says Post Office recently announced a short, final Fujitsu contract extension to maintain continuity while Accenture takes over Horizon support.
fixes.reason: The evidence establishes an announcement, not the extension's commencement.

fixes.was: It could easily be turned on cloud and software providers. Ministers' reliance on 'commercially sensitive' answers may increase pressure for more transparency
fixes.now: The answers describe supplier-risk management and the Post Office's transition arrangements. HMRC does not disclose detailed contract exit and contingency arrangements.
fixes.reason: Removed predictions about future questioning and political pressure.

fixes.was: open-source software must get equal consideration with proprietary options, and that 'code built with public money should be open and reusable by default'
fixes.now: the Government is committed to giving open-source software equal consideration alongside proprietary options. It states: 'Code built with public money should be open and reusable by default.'
fixes.reason: Preserved the answer's distinction between a policy commitment and requirements to demonstrate consideration, and reproduced the quotation accurately.

fixes.was: [redacted supplier-specific prediction]; Expectations on open source and portability may also tighten in spend controls.
fixes.now: The answer identifies supplier dependency, portability and interoperability as risks managed jointly through technical and commercial work. It cites the National Cloud Infrastructure Programme's aims of competition, resilience and choice.
fixes.reason: The evidence does not establish a principal procurement lever, effects on named suppliers or future tightening of controls.

fixes.was: [redacted product-specific wording]
fixes.now: FCDO lists African supply-chain contact routes
fixes.reason: Retained the same supply-chain item and its programme facts without references excluded from public publication or product-ownership claims.

fixes.was: Members also referred to hybrid threats, including cyber attacks and online disinformation.
fixes.now: Members also discussed hybrid threats, including cyber attacks.
fixes.reason: Cyber attacks are explicitly mentioned in the supplied extracts; online disinformation is not.

fixes.was: This is of limited direct relevance. The bill would change the legal risk around user speech on online platforms, including [redacted product reference]
fixes.now: The debate connects protection against abusive litigation with speech on social media. Members from different parties expressed support for the bill.
fixes.reason: Removed audience-specific relevance language and an unsupported application to a particular platform.

fixes.was: The AI Minister (Kanishka Narayan) said OpenAI has committed £100 million and Anthropic up to £100 million in compute and model credits
fixes.now: Kanishka Narayan said OpenAI has committed £100 million in compute and model credits and Anthropic up to £100 million in model credits
fixes.reason: Corrected the type of Anthropic credits. The supplied evidence names the answering minister but does not explicitly establish his personal ministerial title.

fixes.was: He said the Prime Minister's AI Taskforce has no role in departments' choice of AI supplier
fixes.now: Asked about the Prime Minister's AI Taskforce's role in supplier choice, he said individual contracting authorities are responsible for their procurement decisions within procurement legislation.
fixes.reason: Responsibility for individual decisions does not establish that the Taskforce has no role.

fixes.was: The Taskforce will not publish regular milestones. He would not say whether a new AI strategy is planned.
fixes.now: The Taskforce does not intend to publish regular milestones; progress and key milestones will be communicated when appropriate. The answer on a possible new AI strategy did not confirm whether one is planned.
fixes.reason: Restored the qualification and provision for updates, and replaced the implication of deliberate refusal with a neutral description.

fixes.was: [redacted commercial framing]; AI buying remains devolved to individual departments rather than steered centrally
fixes.now: The answers describe credits for the AI Biosecurity Lab and contracting authorities' procurement responsibilities. They do not rule out a wider role for the AI Taskforce.
fixes.reason: Removed commercial positioning, the inaccurate shared description of the credits and an unsupported conclusion about central steering.

fixes.was: The Government will not publish how much has been spent, because the details are commercially sensitive.
fixes.now: The answer does not give a total spent to date and says the Government does not publish commercially sensitive details of how individual companies structure their investments over time.
fixes.reason: The answer's non-disclosure statement concerns individual companies' investment arrangements, not an explicit refusal to publish any aggregate spending figure.

fixes.was: Opposition scrutiny ... could put investors' delivery under the spotlight. The 6GW figure remains the benchmark for data-centre planning and grid debates.
fixes.now: The answers distinguish forecast compute demand and committed investment from expenditure already incurred. No spending total is supplied.
fixes.reason: Removed a predicted political effect and an unsupported claim that the forecast is the benchmark used in planning and grid debates.

fixes.was: data centres to come under NIS; data-centre operators face Ofcom oversight ... the Covenant's tests are being turned into expectations
fixes.now: proposed NIS regulation; The Covenant encourages data centres to meet its tests. The bill would introduce Ofcom-regulated security and resilience requirements for relevant data centres.
fixes.reason: Distinguished voluntary expectations and proposed legislation from duties already in force.

fixes.was: The commitment fee will affect the cost and timing of UK data-centre grid connections. The question on union membership shows the Science and Technology Committee is interested in working practices at Big Tech firms.
fixes.now: The fee remains an Ofgem proposal awaiting a decision. Dame Chi's separate question seeks the Government's assessment of trade union membership in frontier AI and Big Tech companies.
fixes.reason: The fee is not finalised, and an individual member's question is not evidence of a committee position.

fixes.was: This aims to show local opposition to data centres and grid infrastructure within the governing party. An answer could put local resistance to data-centre growth on the record.
fixes.now: The question seeks a count of Labour MPs who have raised constituency infrastructure concerns. No answer is supplied.
fixes.reason: Removed an inferred partisan motive and the equation of unspecified concerns with opposition.

fixes.was: The new national cyber programmes and expanded public-sector AI cyber defence are likely to involve procurement where security vendors and cloud providers will compete.
fixes.now: The answer records an indicative cyber-cost estimate and the Budget's cyber-defence funding priorities. It supplies no procurement details.
fixes.reason: The evidence does not establish competitions, bidders or procurement opportunities.

fixes.was: The UK will set the international AI security agenda in 2027. Industry input on AI system security and critical-infrastructure resilience is likely to be sought.
fixes.now: The answer commits to placing AI at the heart of the UK Presidency but does not confirm the three specific security priorities asked about.
fixes.reason: Removed an overstated international role and an unsupported prediction of industry consultation.

fixes.was: The AI Minister said there is currently 'no clear evidence' of widespread job losses from AI
fixes.now: Kanishka Narayan said there is currently 'no clear evidence' of widespread job displacement attributable to AI across the UK labour market
fixes.reason: Restored the answer's scope and avoided attributing an unverified personal ministerial title.

fixes.was: its ... procurement framework will be available from September 2027. Schools must use it ... A mandatory national framework
fixes.now: its ... procurement framework is expected to be available from September 2027. Schools are expected to award their next MIS contract through the framework when existing contracts expire.
fixes.reason: The answer expresses expectations, not a guaranteed launch or an evidenced mandatory legal requirement; it also allows extensions to bridge the period before availability.

fixes.was: Rules on workplace monitoring could affect productivity, analytics and AI tools used by employers. The employment status consultation ... may be of interest to platform businesses.
fixes.now: The answers describe consultations on workplace monitoring and employment status. The latter closes on 8 January 2027; no final outcomes of those consultations are supplied.
fixes.reason: Removed speculative product effects and audience-oriented relevance.

fixes.was: guidance requires secondary pupils to learn ... Digital and AI literacy is entering the statutory curriculum, a natural area for skills partnerships.
fixes.now: schools have been required to follow the revised statutory guidance since September; it says secondary pupils should learn ... Existing statutory guidance covers AI and deepfakes; wider digital and media literacy reforms are to be included in curriculum consultation.
fixes.reason: Distinguished obligations on schools, the guidance's learning expectations and proposed wider curriculum reforms. Removed an unsupported partnership opportunity.

fixes.was: Shared data infrastructure and the National Data Library are likely future platform and procurement opportunities for public-sector data and AI.
fixes.now: The answer describes common standards and infrastructure intended to improve public-sector data discovery and reuse. It gives no procurement details.
fixes.reason: The evidence does not establish future platform competitions or procurement opportunities.

fixes.was: Sovereign public compute remains a funded priority. It is relevant to the balance between publicly owned and commercial cloud compute.
fixes.now: The answer records a national research-computing funding commitment alongside maintenance of existing research facilities.
fixes.reason: The evidence does not establish ownership arrangements, a cloud-compute policy balance or a specifically sovereign-AI purpose.

fixes.was: the 2.5 million operational images used to test industry algorithms; likely knock-on effects for assurance requirements in public-sector AI contracts
fixes.now: citing an earlier answer, she asked about the source and lawful processing basis of 2.5 million operational images used to test industry algorithms; The questions seek testing and data-processing details. No answers are supplied.
fixes.reason: Attributed the image figure to the question's reference and removed predicted effects on contracts.

fixes.was: whether an independent regulator or ombudsman should handle complaints ... could cover app stores, marketplaces and professional networks
fixes.now: whether the Government has considered establishing an independent regulator or ombudsman to investigate complaints and enforce compliance without court action
fixes.reason: The question asks whether establishing a body has been considered. It does not establish the scope of a future body's jurisdiction.

fixes.was: This signals that ministers are open to safety-by-design duties on connected consumer devices, which could later extend to AI-enabled hardware.
fixes.now: The wearable-technology answer describes safety and privacy expectations and consideration of existing safeguards. It does not announce new duties.
fixes.reason: Removed an unsupported prediction of legal duties and their extension to AI hardware.

fixes.was: the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 bans unfair commercial practices
fixes.now: the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 prohibits unfair commercial practices, including misleading actions and omissions likely to affect the average consumer's transactional decision
fixes.reason: Restored the material qualification in the answer.

fixes.was: an area where online platforms face pressure on harmful and fraudulent ads

fixes.reason: The supplied answer does not establish pressure on platforms or discuss fraudulent advertisements generally.

fixes.was: Government data-handling failures keep data security and information governance high on the agenda, the context for public-sector demand for secure platforms.
